title: Расспросы Кости о слабостях Ильи  (Questioning Kostya About Ilya's Weaknesses)

segments.t: Pretending that he wants to bury the hatchet with Ilya, Max casually asks Kostya what kind of things his old friend loves most. Trusting his roommate completely, Kostya gives Max the exact information he needs to prepare a cruel surprise for Ilya.
Не знаю, как к нему подойти, чтобы помириться.
А ты что, реально хочешь с ним помириться?
Слушай, что он любит вообще, а?
Now let's go back through the conversation line by line.
Не знаю, как к нему подойти, чтобы помириться.
'I do not know how to approach him to make peace.' Kostya strikes a direct angle on the spot, using "znayu" (from "znat", "know") alongside "kak" ("how") to shape the meaning.
'Maybe I should invite him out for a beer, huh?' Ilya inquires earnestly in the scene, linking "mozhet" ("can"), "pivo" ("beer"), and "priglasit" ("to invite") in one brisk exchange.
'Well, maybe.' Kostya keeps a lively mood in their talk, using "mozhet" (from "moch", "can") alongside "nu" ("oh, come on") to shape the meaning.
А ты что, реально хочешь с ним помириться?

'Wait, do you seriously want to make peace with him?' Ilya inquires boldly at this point, anchoring the Russian line on "realno" ("really possible") and "khochesh" ("do you want") without extra filler.
'Well yeah, that is why I am asking you.' Kostya conveys a calm line for Ilya, putting "poetomu" ("that's why") alongside "sprashivayu" ("am asking") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
Слушай, что он любит вообще, а?

'Listen, what does he like in general?' Ilya checks openly for Max's benefit, combining the conversational booster "voobshche" ("in general, overall") with "slushay" ("listen") to give the line its natural spoken rhythm.
'Oh, he likes all kinds of things.' Kostya sets a brisk tempo right away, anchoring the Russian line on "lyubit" ("loves") and "da" ("yes") without extra filler.
'Actually, this will be even better.' Ilya takes a warm rhythm in their talk, linking "luchshe" ("better"), "tak" ("so"), and "vot" ("there, here") in one brisk exchange.
'He is going to love this.' Kostya shows an unhurried tempo in the conversation, pairing "ponravitsya" ("will please") with "yemu" ("him") so the "-sya" ending carries the action.
'You are welcome.' Ilya conveys a candid attitude in the scene, weaving "ne" ("not") together with "za" ("for") just the way native speakers do.
'Thanks, Kostyan.' Max brings a wry mood across the room, joining "spasibo" ("thank you") to "kostyan" ("Kostyan") so every word pulls its weight.
'Alright, I am off.' Ilya sets a wry tack in front of Max, building the phrase around "davay" ("let's") and "poshel" ("go, off you go") for a crisp, natural delivery.
'Just a little token.' Kostya chooses an honest course at once, putting "no" ("but") alongside "eto" ("this") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
Не знаю, как к нему подойти, чтобы помириться.
А ты что, реально хочешь с ним помириться?
Слушай, что он любит вообще, а?
That wraps up this scene as pretending he wants to make peace with Ilya, Max tricks Kostya into telling him what Ilya cares about most so he can strike where it hurts. See you next time!
